newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil premiums directionless, volume thin.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil premiums directionless, volume thin.

text.p: NWE gas oil premiums were mostly unchanged but directionless in lacklustre business on Friday with traders playing a waiting game to see if the main long on November IPE futures delivery would come to the market.

"There is nothing around for prompt," said one trader. "It's clearly the feeling that people want a little bit to play a game against (the dominant long), thinking that they might come out to sell. But perhaps they won't."
"It all depends on the long," another trader said. "If 200,000-300,000 tonnes comes onto the market premiums will collapse."
The trading house with the bulk of the record high 865,100 tonne delivery indicated it felt it had no need to sell into the market and that it was confident it had homes for the material.
Dec IPE firmed $0.25 to $219.50 a tonne, off an earlier high of $221.50. A barge of low sulphur winter grade (-7/-22) traded at Dec +$14/15, $2 firmer, indicating tighter fundamentals.
A barge of 0.2 percent sulphur heating oil was done at Dec +$225/22.50, then equivalent to Dec +$5/5.50, unchanged.
Low sulphur cargoes were unchanged at Dec +$16/17. Heating oil was seen at around Dec +$6-10.
